doc.title: Bill Goodwin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 28, 2025

title: Turning down Bill Evans, Horace Silver and Herb Alpert for Phil Woods
summary: Why he chose to join Phil's new band over several offers, with Steve Gilmore's comment about being typecast.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Well I pretty much always had that — there have been instances where I was pretty sure I wasn't going to do so well and I would turn the gig down with that. Sorry that I did now. One was to play the Leonard Bernstein mass and that was because of Chuck Israels, another bass player, was always recommending me for stuff. And so it is what it is. I knew that, you know it was just kismet, you know? And the phone rings and you know I’ve had so many offers. You know, say really good paying, good gig offers that I had to turn down because of joining Phil’s group and right at the same time Marty Morell left Bill Evans and Bill called me. I was the first drummer he called and I went and played with him for about ten days. He offered me the gig and I turned it down.
You know Steve Gilmore said that he thinks he missed some work because people thought oh well he plays with Phil Woods. He’s not going to be able to do anything else.

Well Steve was very busy before he was working with Phil doing Broadway shows, subbing and playing with a lot of people. And he, you know, it could be, but I just had to make that choice. Because I’d always wanted to play with Bill Evans. That was a band that was — traveled all the time. And that’s what we were getting into with Phil, and you know that was a band that nobody knew really. We started to get well known, we started to get gigs, and it was something like, you know you’d get an opportunity to start something from, you know square one and make it happen, you know it turned out to be 40 years. I mean that’s pretty good man. But I turned down — let’s see — the only guy that I turned down, Bill Evans, Horace Silver, and Herb Alpert and the Tijuana Brass.
Yeah. They were all my friends.

They recommended me and I went and auditioned for Herb Alpert. He said, “Well you can have the gig, you can certainly do the gig but I want you to move back to L.A.” I said, “No, man, I’m not going to do that.”
